reason: A short `\u` escape on line 2 of a long string reports line 2, column 4 (#521; `_unescape`, `_Lexer.locate`). It raises from the hex-digit branch of `_unescape`, not the unknown-escape statement of test_provn_lexer.py::test_string_escape_error_position, so it stays out of that merge.

Short hex, lowercase hex, non-scalar values, unknown IRI escapes and IRI-forbidden characters each raise at the escape (#521, #729; `_unescape`, `_Lexer.locate`, `_IRI_FORBIDDEN`), through `_Lexer.string_token` and `_Lexer.iri_token`. `_Lexer.locate` places the error. Rows share statements, since the rows that reach the `_HEX_DIGITS` branch raise from one statement and the four unknown IRI escapes from the one `kind == "IRI"` statement. The rows stay for their own input shapes, not for their own branches.

A raw CR inside a short string or a quoted name makes it unterminated, because `_SHORT_STRING` and `_QNAME_LITERAL`, matched in `_Lexer.string_token` and `_Lexer.qname_literal_token`, exclude CR. Its rows are the unescaped counterpart of the backslash-CR rows of test_provn_lexer.py::test_malformed_input_reports_position.
`\u` and `\U` escapes decode in strings and IRIs, and `\\u` stays literal (#521, #729; `_unescape`, `_ESCAPE`).

`//` and `/* */` comments are dropped between tokens by `_Lexer.tokens`, which applies `_SKIP`. This is the plain case, a line comment and a multi-line block comment between two names. A `_SKIP` without its comment alternatives fails this test and also test_provn_lexer.py::test_line_comment_ends_at_cr_not_just_lf, test_provn_lexer.py::test_ws_and_spaces_inside_comments_strings_and_iris_are_not_errors and the block-comment row of test_provn_lexer.py::test_line_and_column_tracking. Its lone-CR sibling is test_provn_lexer.py::test_line_comment_ends_at_cr_not_just_lf.

A backslash escape in a local part is accepted for exactly the PN_CHARS_ESC characters and rejected, at column 6, for every other printable ASCII character and two Latin-1 ones. `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token` matches `_QNAME` and `_qname_value` unescapes it, and `_Lexer.next_token` raises for the rejected characters. The escape sits mid-name (`ex:na\{ch}me`), so it meets `_LOCAL_CONT`, where test_provn_lexer.py::test_local_part_and_prefix_spellings puts it at the start or end of a local part. Each row is a different character against the one class `_ESC`. Removing `;` from `_ESC` fails only the `;` row, and adding `q` fails only the `q` row.
A 5000-digit integer raises `ProvNSyntaxError` naming the digit limit, not `ValueError` (`_Lexer._int_value`). A raw `int()` would crash the reader on hostile input.
`"a"@` raises "invalid language tag" from `_Lexer.langtag_token` (`_LANGTAG`). It guards the failure branch of the tag reader.
An IRI may hold U+00A0 but not `\x01` (`_IRI` and `_IRI_EXCLUDED`, matched in `_Lexer.iri_token`). It guards both the accept and the reject side of the IRI character class.

`_Lexer.next_token` hands `@en` to `_Lexer.langtag_token` after a string, so `"a place"@en` gives a STRING token then a LANGTAG token. `ex:a@b` stays one NAME, because `@` is a name character (`_PN_CHARS_OTHER` in prov.identifier) and `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token` reads the whole name before any `@` branch is reached. The test does not pin the after-a-string guard. With `and self.previous is TokenKind.STRING` deleted from `_Lexer.next_token`, this module stayed green, and in the whole suite only test_pygments.py::test_snippet_is_accepted_by_the_reader failed.

Token line and column after LF, CRLF and CR breaks, inside long strings and inside block comments (`_Lexer.advance_lines`, `_Lexer._line_after`, `_Lexer.emit`, `_LINEBREAK`). Each row has its own break kind or token type, so a fault in one counting path fails one row.

A `//` comment ends at a lone CR, as the Recommendation's comment note says (`_SKIP`, matched in `_Lexer.tokens`). A lone CR is its own input shape beside test_provn_lexer.py::test_comments_are_skipped.

`_QNAME` and `_qname_value`, applied by `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token` and `_Lexer.name_token`, turn one spelling of a name into a (prefix, local) pair: a percent escape (`_PERCENT`), an escaped dot or colon at the end of a local part (`_LOCAL_LAST`), an escaped hyphen that is the only local character (`_LOCAL_START`, because a lone escape matches the start class and never the last), an inner dot in a local part (`_LOCAL_CONT`) or in a prefix (`_PN_PREFIX`), and a bare name with the empty prefix. Removing the escape from `_LOCAL_LAST` fails the escaped-dot and escaped-colon rows, removing it from `_LOCAL_START` fails the escaped-hyphen row, and removing `_PERCENT` from `_LOCAL_CONT` fails the percent row. Folds in test_provn_lexer.py::test_percent_encoding_is_kept_verbatim, test_provn_lexer.py::test_escaped_dot_is_kept, test_provn_lexer.py::test_inner_dot_is_part_of_the_name, test_provn_lexer.py::test_escaped_colon_at_end_of_local_part, test_provn_lexer.py::test_escaped_hyphen_in_local_part (section 3.8 example), test_provn_lexer.py::test_prefix_with_inner_dot_is_still_accepted and test_provn_lexer.py::test_bare_local_name_has_empty_prefix. All seven asserted `values(text) == [(prefix, local)]`, so only the input and the expected pair moved into rows and nothing was lost. The prefix row still guards `_PN_PREFIX` against over-rejection beside test_provn_lexer.py::test_prefix_cannot_end_in_a_dot.

A million trailing dots fail within a time bound, so `_LOCAL_LAST` and `_PN_LOCAL`, matched through `_QNAME` in `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token`, stay linear. A quadratic back-off would pass every test that has no time bound.

Each malformed input raises `ProvNSyntaxError` with the right line, column and the text "line N, column M" (`_Lexer.error`, `_Lexer.tokens`, `_Lexer.next_token`, `_Lexer.string_token`, `_Lexer.iri_token`, `_Lexer.qname_literal_token`, `_Lexer.name_token`, `_split_qname`, `_unescape`). Two rows raise from helpers. The `'a\<CR>b'` row raises from `_split_qname`, called by `_Lexer.qname_literal_token`, and the `"a\<CR>b"` row from `_unescape`, while `ex:a:b` raises from `_Lexer.name_token`. The whitespace rows (#509) put each of the 24 `NON_WS_SPACES` characters, and a final NBSP row, at a token start, so they meet only the classes that begin a token. Planting all 24 characters in `_PN_CHARS_U` (read by `_LOCAL_START`) fails 25 rows of this test. Planting them in the lexer's `_PN_CHARS` fails none, and neither does planting them in `_PN_CHARS_BASE` of prov.identifier (read by `_PN_PREFIX`). The rows are different characters against the same classes, so a class edit can fail many rows at once.
`-` alone is a marker, `-5` is an integer and `- 5` is a marker then an integer, which depends on `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token` running before the marker branch of `_Lexer.next_token`.
Arabic-Indic and fullwidth digits are name characters, not integers, because PROV-N DIGIT is `[0-9]` (`_INT`, `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token`). The two rows are two code-point blocks.
The error for U+00A0 reads "U+00A0 is not PROV-N whitespace" (#509; `_Lexer.next_token`). test_provn.py::test_reader_rejects reaches the same message through the parser, a different entry point.

`NON_WS_SPACES` plus U+1680 equals every `str.isspace` code point outside space, tab, CR and LF (#509). It runs no `src/prov` code and keeps the oracle list behind test_provn_lexer.py::test_malformed_input_reports_position complete.
U+1680 starts a name and is not a separator (#509; `_Lexer.next_token`, which comments on U+1680).

The derived PN_CHARS classes equal the Recommendation's literal ranges over every non-surrogate code point (`_PN_CHARS_U` and `_PN_CHARS` in provn_lexer, and `_PN_CHARS_BASE` and `_PN_CHARS_ESC` in prov.identifier). `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token` applies them through `_QNAME`, but the test runs no function and compares the constants. The contract is real and the test reaches it through private names.

A prefix that ends in a dot is rejected at or after the dot (PROV-N PN_PREFIX; `_PN_PREFIX` in `_QNAME`, matched in `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token`). It pairs with the inner-dot prefix row of test_provn_lexer.py::test_local_part_and_prefix_spellings.

`entity(bbc:)` reads `bbc:` as a name with an empty local part, the Recommendation's own example, through the optional local part of `_QNAME` in `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token`. It asserts the first four tokens of a statement, so it is not a row of test_provn_lexer.py::test_local_part_and_prefix_spellings.

`ProvNSyntaxError` is a public exception and survives pickle and deepcopy with its line, column and message intact (`ProvNSyntaxError.__reduce__`). A `__reduce__` that dropped an argument would break copying across processes.

A quoted name that `_QNAME_FULL` rejects raises from `_split_qname`, called by `_Lexer.qname_literal_token`, and `_Lexer.locate` (given the offset of the end of the partial `_QNAME` match) puts the error at column 5 for a space after a bare name, column 8 for a space inside a prefixed name, and column 8 for a trailing dot. Folds in test_provn_lexer.py::test_invalid_qname_literal_raises, test_provn_lexer.py::test_qname_literal_error_position_is_the_first_invalid_character and test_provn_lexer.py::test_qname_literal_trailing_dot_raises. Every input and assertion stays, so nothing was lost. The two rows with no message check pass `match=None`, which pytest treats as no check, as the rows of test_provn_lexer.py::test_string_escape_error_position do. The row `space-after-bare-name` is named for its input, because a bare `not` alone is a valid name.
A quoted qualified name decodes `\'` into its local part through `_Lexer.qname_literal_token`, `_split_qname` and `_qname_value`.

A bare trailing dot on a local part raises at the dot's column, because a PN_LOCAL cannot end in a dot (`_LOCAL_LAST`, `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token`, `_Lexer.next_token`). The position check is exact where test_provn_lexer.py::test_prefix_cannot_end_in_a_dot checks `>=`, and this input is a local part, not a prefix.

An unknown `\q` escape raises from the one statement in `_unescape` that rejects it, and `_Lexer.locate` puts the error at the escape: column 2 of `"\q"`, column 6 inside a short string, and line 2 column 4 in a long string. Folds in test_provn_lexer.py::test_unknown_string_escape_raises, test_provn_lexer.py::test_string_escape_error_position_is_inside_the_literal and test_provn_lexer.py::test_string_escape_error_position_spans_lines_in_a_long_string. Every input and assertion stays, and `match=None` asserts what leaving out `match` did, so nothing was lost. The issue citation of the classifier (#521, the code point escapes) does not match these inputs.

Short strings decode `\\`, `\"` and `\t` in `_unescape` through `_STRING_ESCAPES`, called from `_Lexer.string_token`. The long-string row holds no backslash and pins that `_LONG_STRING` keeps inner quotes and a newline; removing the inner-quote alternative from `_LONG_STRING` fails only this test in the module. A lost `\\` entry in `_STRING_ESCAPES` fails this test and also the `\\u00E9` row of test_provn_lexer.py::test_code_point_escapes_are_decoded.

`Token` is public through `__all__`, and hashing and comparing it by field is the contract. The test's own comment calls a per-instance `__dict__` overhead. A `Token` that lost `unsafe_hash` would stop hashing by field, and one that lost `slots` would gain a `__dict__`. Dropping either from the dataclass fails this test.

`tokenize` gives each token class (name, string, integer, datetime, IRI and the punctuation) its `TokenKind`, through the dispatch order of `_Lexer.next_token` and `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token`. The rows are plain tuples of input and expected kinds. Moving the marker branch of `_Lexer.next_token` ahead of the `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token` call fails the `-42` row, which would otherwise read as a marker and an integer.

`%%` between tokens is the typed-literal marker, read by `_Lexer.next_token`, and `%41` at the start of a local part stays in the name through `_PERCENT` in `_LOCAL_START`, applied by `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token`. Changing the `%%` check in `_Lexer.next_token` to a single `%` leaves this test green and fails only the `"x" %` row of test_provn_lexer.py::test_malformed_input_reports_position. Removing the `%%` branch fails the first assertion here and the `%%` row of test_provn_lexer.py::test_token_kinds, and removing `_PERCENT` from `_LOCAL_START` fails the `ex:%41b` assertion alone.

Non-ASCII names tokenise through `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token`, where the final `é` of `café` matches `_LOCAL_LAST` through `_PN_CHARS`, and a non-ASCII string through `_SHORT_STRING` in `_Lexer.string_token`. A `_LOCAL_LAST` limited to ASCII fails this test and the two rows of test_provn_lexer.py::test_non_ascii_digits_are_names_not_integers. The judge ruled that it stays unfolded, because the string assertion pins a STRING token, and a row under test_provn_lexer.py::test_local_part_and_prefix_spellings would label it a name spelling. The maintainer accepted the ruling.
An open `/*` raises "unterminated comment" at the opener, from the `startswith("/*")` check in `_Lexer.tokens`.
Tab, CRLF, NBSP and U+3000 inside comments, strings and IRIs, and between tokens, raise nothing (#509; `_SKIP`, `_Lexer.next_token`). It guards against over-rejection beside the whitespace rule.
